first.rationale: Two declines (onboarding -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and the inherited record has three converging beliefs there (memory_86 onboarding shortening, memory_31 signup simplification, memory_91 in-product activation messaging). Onboarding is upstream of activation, so fixing it plausibly recovers both, which is why simplify_onboarding is my current intent. Verification triage: I spend the two pulls on the beliefs that are simultaneously most load-bearing for this decision and weakest for the stated objective of SUSTAINABLE LONG-TERM QUALIFIED revenue. (1) memory_86 is the direct foundation of my intended action, yet as recorded it only evidences completion rates, time-to-value, and 'early product adoption' — all proxy metrics. None of those is qualified revenue, and shortening onboarding or cutting fields can lift completion by admitting lower-intent accounts, so the archived record needs to show whether downstream retention/revenue was measured or merely assumed. (2) memory_73 is the strongest competing pull given the competitor's entry pricing, and it is the single riskiest belief here: 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' is silent on churn, discount cohort quality, and margin persistence, which is exactly the failure mode where short-run wins invert into long-run value destruction. If its source shows only a short observation window, discounting is disqualified as this week's slot regardless of competitive urgency. I deliberately do not spend a pull on memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) because it does not address either observed decline, or on memory_57 (referrals), which presupposes a healthy activation base that is currently degrading. Note the base rates may have shifted: these records are 15-64 days old and the competitor launch is new, so a prior lift is not a guarantee of a present lift. I therefore run this as a standard experiment with holdout and explicit downstream guardrails (30/90-day retention, paid conversion, revenue per activated account), not as a broad rollout, and I will not treat completion-rate movement alone as success. If memory_86's source turns out to rest only on proxy metrics, I will keep simplify_onboarding but shrink to a guarded test and instrument revenue quality more heavily rather than switching to promotional pricing.

final.rationale: Both pulls paid off, in opposite directions. memory_86 held up and then some: exp_86 did not stop at proxy metrics — it carried completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days through to 30-day retention +3%. That is the durability evidence I was worried might be missing, so simplify_onboarding survives verification as a real value-creating lever rather than a funnel-metric artifact. memory_73 failed exactly at the predicted failure mode: signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% sat on top of 30-day retention -12%, and the source record itself says the discounted cohort does not survive first renewal and warns against generalizing targeted discounting. The compressed memory summary ('strong acquisition and revenue lift') had silently dropped the retention collapse and the explicit do-not-generalize caveat. Under an objective of SUSTAINABLE long-term qualified revenue, promotional_pricing is now disqualified, and I am noting that competitive urgency is precisely the pressure that would have made me misread that memory — matching the competitor's entry pricing would buy a quarter of signups and hand back the renewal cohort. So: simplify_onboarding, aimed at the upstream cause of both observed declines (onboarding -4% feeding activation -6%), with memory_31 and memory_91 as converging support for the same funnel stage. Standard experiment with holdout, not broad rollout, for three reasons I want to keep visible rather than assume away: exp_86 is 24 days stale and predates the competitor launch, so the base rate may have shifted; exp_86's retention evidence stops at 30 days while the real question is renewal-cycle value, which is exactly where discounting looked fine at first and then inverted; and the current declines may have a cause other than the flow itself (traffic-mix shift from competitor pressure), in which case flow changes will underdeliver. Guardrails: 30/90-day retention, paid conversion, and revenue per activated account, with completion rate explicitly NOT accepted as standalone success. If lift appears in completion but not in downstream revenue quality, I treat that as a negative result. I also recommend writing the exp_73 retention finding and caveat back into durable memory so the next session does not re-inherit the sanitized version.
